dataset.name: Electrical resistivity tomography, electromagnetic data, and permafrost cores acquired near Utqiagvik, Alaska, 2011-2015
description: Subsurface electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), electromagnetic data, and permafrost cores were acquired between 2011 and 2015 within the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) on the Alaskan Arctic Coastal Plain, approximately 4 miles from the Beaufort Sea near Utqiaġvik, Alaska. This dataset has been used to improve the quantification of subsurface properties and the understanding of co-variability between subsurface and surface properties. The reference list attached to this data archive names studies and other measurements associated with this dataset.

Measurements were acquired at various locations, including along a 475 m long, 20 m wide corridor (named L2 or Z0) and a 500 m long, 40 m wide corridor (AB), both covering various polygon types. ERT surveys were conducted using 0.5 m electrode spacing and a roll-along acquisition strategy along the 475 and 500 m long transects. Electromagnetic data were acquire using a portable low-induction electromagnetic sensor (EM38). Cores were acquired at several location along the transect to obtain depth profile of permafrost physical properties. The measurement locations are provided using NAD83 (2011), the 2012 geoid, and UTM Zone 4 North coordinates. The dataset contains 4 *.csv data files and 5 *.csv metadata files.

The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic) was a 15-year research effort (2012-2027) to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. NGEE Arctic was supported by the Department of Energy’s Office of Biological and Environmental Research. The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska, and 2) multiple areas in the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska. Through observations, experiments, and synthesis with existing datasets, NGEE Arctic provided an enhanced knowledge base for multi-scale modeling and contributed to improved process representation at global pan-Arctic scales within the Department of Energy’s Earth system Model (the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, or E3SM), and specifically within the E3SM Land Model component (ELM).
